entities.name: Melioidosis
entities.description: Severe, life-threatening tropical infectious disease caused by the environmental Gram-negative bacterium Burkholderia pseudomallei, characterized by protean manifestations ranging from localized abscesses and severe necrotizing pneumonia to fulminant bacteremic septic shock, especially in patients with diabetes mellitus.

entities.name: Burkholderia pseudomallei
entities.description: Aerobic, motile, oxidase-positive, Gram-negative saprophytic bacillus exhibiting a characteristic bipolar 'safety-pin' staining appearance; survives intracellularly and persists in tropical wet soil and water.

entities.name: Wet Soil and Surface Water Inoculation During Monsoons
entities.description: Direct percutaneous inoculation of broken skin or minor abrasions with Burkholderia pseudomallei from wet tropical agricultural soils, mud, or surface water during monsoons (e.g., rice farming, walking barefoot, gardening).

entities.name: Aerosol Inhalation During Tropical Storms and Cyclones
entities.description: Inhalation of aerosolized Burkholderia pseudomallei in soil dust and water droplets during severe weather events such as typhoons, monsoons, cyclones, and near-drowning events, leading to rapid-onset severe pulmonary melioidosis.

entities.name: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Host Predisposition
entities.description: The single most critical predisposing host comorbidity, present in 40–60% of all melioidosis cases, driven by neutrophil oxidative burst impairment and defective phagocytosis.

entities.name: Hazardous Alcohol Consumption Host Predisposition
entities.description: Chronic heavy alcohol misuse present in 15–30% of melioidosis patients, impairing alveolar macrophage function and cell-mediated immunity, predisposing to bacteremia and severe sepsis.

entities.name: Chronic Kidney Disease Host Predisposition
entities.description: Underlying chronic renal insufficiency present in 10–25% of cases, conferring an independent high risk for bacteremic melioidosis, acute renal deterioration, and fatal septic shock.

entities.name: Endemic Tropical Geographic Exposure
entities.description: Residence in or travel to core endemic zones, predominantly Northern Australia (Top End, Kimberley) and Southeast Asia (Thailand, Vietnam, Cambodia, Laos, Malaysia, Singapore), South Asia (India), Latin America, or the US Gulf Coast.

entities.name: Honeycomb Swiss-Cheese Splenic Microabscesses
entities.description: Multiple small, discrete coalescing hypoechoic microabscesses throughout the splenic and hepatic parenchyma producing a pathognomonic Swiss-cheese or honeycomb pattern on POCUS ultrasound or admission CT.

entities.name: Suppurative Parotitis in Pediatric Patients
entities.description: Acute, painful, unilateral preauricular swelling and abscess formation representing a pathognomonic hallmark of melioidosis in children in endemic Southeast Asian regions (accounting for up to 30% of pediatric cases).

entities.name: Prostatic Abscess in Adult Males
entities.description: Acute pelvic/perineal pain, dysuria, hesitancy, and urinary retention secondary to suppurative prostatic microabscesses or macroabscesses, present in 18–30% of adult male melioidosis patients in endemic regions.

entities.name: Acute Necrotizing Cavitary Pneumonia
entities.description: High spiking fevers, profuse night sweats, purulent productive cough, pleuritic pain, and hemoptysis with rapid pulmonary cavitation on plain radiography, representing the primary presentation in ~50% of cases.

entities.name: Neurological Melioidosis with Brainstem Encephalitis
entities.description: Severe neuromelioidosis presenting with rhombencephalitis, peripheral facial palsy (cranial nerve VII), flaccid tetraparesis, or cerebellar ataxia, often presenting with normal initial brain CT imaging.

entities.name: Marked Neutrophilic Leukocytosis with Toxic Granulation
entities.description: Admission triage CBC showing total WBC 15,000–35,000/µL with >15% band forms (bandemia) and toxic granulation, signaling overwhelming bacterial pyogenic infection (or profound leukopenia <3,000/µL in lethal septic shock).

entities.name: Massive Acute-Phase Reactive Protein Elevation
entities.description: Striking admission inflammatory markers with C-reactive protein (CRP) >150–300 mg/L, ESR >80 mm/h, and procalcitonin markedly elevated (>2–10 ng/mL), differentiating acute melioidosis from viral infections and subacute mycobacterial disease.

entities.name: Severe Admission Hyperglycemia and Unmasked Diabetes
entities.description: Marked admission blood glucose elevation (>200–400 mg/dL) with elevated HbA1c (>9–12%), frequently unmasking previously undiagnosed Type 2 diabetes mellitus at triage.

entities.name: Upper Lobe Infiltrates Without Mediastinal Lymphadenopathy on Chest Radiography
entities.description: Admission plain chest radiograph showing rapid upper-lobe alveolar consolidation, alveolar infiltrate, and thin/thick-walled cavitary lesions without the hilar or mediastinal lymphadenopathy typical of tuberculosis.

entities.name: Bedside Ultrasound Hypoechoic Splenic and Prostatic Fluid Collections
entities.description: Rapid bedside POCUS ultrasound identifying multi-focal small hypoechoic lesions in the spleen and fluid collections in the prostate gland in febrile patients with sepsis.

entities.name: Complete Absence of Tropical Endemic Exposure or Travel
entities.description: Absence of any lifetime travel or residence in known endemic regions (Southeast Asia, Northern Australia, South Asia, tropical Americas, US Gulf Coast) virtually excludes melioidosis in non-laboratory settings.

entities.name: Immunocompetent Host with Zero Environmental Soil or Water Contact
entities.description: A healthy host without diabetes, alcoholism, or chronic kidney disease who has no history of contact with muddy soil, surface water, or severe weather exposure is extraordinarily unlikely to have melioidosis.

entities.name: Normal Inflammatory Markers and Absence of Leukocytosis
entities.description: Completely normal admission CRP (<10 mg/L), normal procalcitonin (<0.1 ng/mL), and normal WBC count without bandemia strongly rules out acute systemic or invasive melioidosis.

entities.name: Rapid Clinical Defervescence on Standard Ceftriaxone or Ampicillin
entities.description: Prompt defervescence and resolution of sepsis or pneumonia within 48–72 hours of empirical treatment with ampicillin, ceftriaxone, or cefotaxime definitively rules out Burkholderia pseudomallei due to uniform intrinsic beta-lactam resistance.

entities.name: Chronic Indolent Progression Over Months with Mediastinal Lymphadenopathy
entities.description: An indolent constitutional course progressing over multiple months accompanied by prominent hilar and mediastinal lymphadenopathy and normal procalcitonin rules out acute pulmonary melioidosis and indicates primary mycobacterial infection.

entities.name: Pulmonary Tuberculosis
entities.description: Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection, the primary look-alike of pulmonary melioidosis presenting with chronic cough, night sweats, weight loss, hemoptysis, and upper lobe cavitary lesions.

entities.name: Community-Acquired Bacterial Pneumonia
entities.description: Acute bacterial pneumonia caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae or Klebsiella pneumoniae, presenting with acute cough, fever, and lobar consolidation.

entities.name: Leptospirosis
entities.description: Zoonotic spirochetal infection caused by Leptospira interrogans acquired via contaminated floodwater, presenting with acute high fever, severe myalgias, and multi-organ dysfunction.

entities.name: Scrub Typhus
entities.description: Vector-borne rickettsial infection caused by Orientia tsutsugamushi transmitted by larval trombiculid mites in rural tropical environments, presenting with acute febrile illness.

entities.name: Intrinsic Resistance to Ceftriaxone Penicillins and Aminoglycosides
entities.description: Uniform chromosomal intrinsic resistance of Burkholderia pseudomallei to penicillins, ampicillin, first- and second-generation cephalosporins, third-generation cephalosporins (ceftriaxone, cefotaxime), macrolides, aminoglycosides, and colistin.

entities.name: Intravenous Ceftazidime Intensive Phase Therapy
entities.description: First-line bactericidal acute intensive intravenous therapy (2 g IV every 6–8 hours or 50 mg/kg up to 2 g Q8H for ≥10–14 days) reducing acute mortality by 50%, characteristically accompanied by a slow median fever clearance of 9–10 days.

entities.name: Intravenous Meropenem Intensive Phase Therapy
entities.description: Preferred carbapenem regimen (1–2 g IV every 8 hours) for critically ill patients presenting with septic shock, deep undrained collections, or neurological melioidosis, conferring rapid bactericidal activity and lower endotoxin release than ceftazidime.

entities.name: Oral Trimethoprim-Sulfamethoxazole Eradication Phase Therapy
entities.description: Definitive oral eradication therapy (TMP-SMX 320/1600 mg BID with oral folic acid for a minimum of 3 to 6 months) essential to eradicate intracellular persisters and prevent recurrence and fatal late relapse ('Vietnam time-bomb' reactivation).

entities.name: Empirical Fluoroquinolone and Macrolide Treatment Failure
entities.description: Ineffective clinical response to fluoroquinolones (ciprofloxacin, ofloxacin) or macrolides (azithromycin), which demonstrate unacceptable failure and relapse rates (up to 29%) in clinical trials.

relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGEN] Melioidosis is caused by Burkholderia pseudomallei, an aerobic, motile, oxidase-positive Gram-negative saprophytic bacillus with bipolar 'safety-pin' staining that persists in tropical soil and surface water.

relationships.target: Wet Soil and Surface Water Inoculation During Monsoons
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Acquired primarily via percutaneous inoculation through broken skin or minor abrasions after direct occupational or recreational exposure to contaminated wet soil, mud, or surface water during tropical monsoons (e.g., rice farming, gardening, walking barefoot).

relationships.target: Aerosol Inhalation During Tropical Storms and Cyclones
relationships.description: [TRANSMITTED_BY] Acquired via inhalation of aerosolized Burkholderia pseudomallei particles and contaminated water droplets during high-humidity monsoons, cyclones, typhoons, and near-drowning events, leading to hyperacute severe pneumonia.

[EXPOSURE_TO] Type 2 diabetes mellitus is the single strongest host susceptibility factor, present in 40–60% of all melioidosis patients due to diabetic neutrophil oxidative burst defects and impaired intracellular bacterial killing.
[EXPOSURE_TO] Hazardous alcohol use is present in 15–30% of patients, impairing alveolar macrophage bactericidal function and predisposing to severe bacteremic dissemination and septic shock.
[EXPOSURE_TO] Underlying chronic renal disease is present in 10–25% of cases, conferring an independent elevated risk for severe bacteremic melioidosis, acute kidney injury, and high mortality.

[EXPOSURE_TO] Exposure requires travel or residence in tropical endemic areas, predominantly Northern Australia, Southeast Asia (Thailand, Vietnam, Cambodia, Laos, Malaysia, Singapore), South Asia (India, Sri Lanka), the tropical Americas, or the US Gulf Coast.

[HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] The presence of multiple small, discrete coalescing microabscesses throughout the splenic and hepatic parenchyma creating a classic 'honeycomb' or 'Swiss-cheese' appearance on abdominal ultrasound or CT is a pathognomonic hallmark strongly ruling in melioidosis.

[HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Acute painful unilateral suppurative parotitis and preauricular abscess in an endemic child (accounting for up to 30% of pediatric melioidosis cases in Thailand and Cambodia) is a cardinal clinical hallmark.

[HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Suppurative prostatic abscess presenting with perineal/pelvic pain, dysuria, hesitancy, and acute urinary retention in adult febrile males in endemic regions occurs in 18–30% of male melioidosis patients.

[HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Acute onset of high spiking fever, profuse drenching night sweats, productive purulent cough, pleuritic chest pain, and hemoptysis with rapid pulmonary cavitation represents the cardinal presentation in approximately 50% of melioidosis patients.

[HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Neuromelioidosis classically presents with rhombencephalitis (brainstem encephalitis), unilateral cranial nerve palsies (especially peripheral CN VII palsy), flaccid tetraparesis, or cerebellar ataxia, often despite normal initial head CT imaging.

relationships.target: Marked Neutrophilic Leukocytosis with Toxic Granulation
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Admission complete blood count demonstrates marked neutrophilic leukocytosis with total WBC 15,000–35,000/µL, prominent toxic left shift (bandemia >15%), and toxic granulation (or severe leukopenia <3,000/µL in fulminant septic shock portending extreme mortality).

[EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Admission laboratory profile exhibits a massive acute-phase systemic response with C-reactive protein (CRP) >150–300 mg/L, ESR >80 mm/h, and procalcitonin markedly elevated (>2–10 ng/mL).

relationships.target: Severe Admission Hyperglycemia and Unmasked Diabetes
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Admission metabolic panel frequently reveals severe hyperglycemia (>200–400 mg/dL) and elevated glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c >9–12%), unmasking previously undiagnosed or poorly controlled Type 2 diabetes mellitus at triage.

relationships.target: Upper Lobe Infiltrates Without Mediastinal Lymphadenopathy on Chest Radiography
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Admission chest radiograph demonstrates upper lobe alveolar consolidation, rapid progression to thin- or thick-walled cavitary lesions, and absence of mediastinal or hilar lymphadenopathy (which distinguishes it from primary tuberculosis).

relationships.target: Bedside Ultrasound Hypoechoic Splenic and Prostatic Fluid Collections
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Bedside POCUS ultrasound detects multiple discrete round hypoechoic parenchymal microabscesses in the spleen and liver, and hypoechoic fluid collections in the prostate gland in febrile septic patients.

relationships.target: Complete Absence of Tropical Endemic Exposure or Travel
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Complete absence of lifetime residence in or travel to known tropical endemic areas (Southeast Asia, Northern Australia, South Asia, Latin America, US Gulf Coast) virtually rules out melioidosis in non-laboratory settings.

relationships.target: Immunocompetent Host with Zero Environmental Soil or Water Contact
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] A healthy host without underlying diabetes, renal disease, or alcohol excess who has had zero exposure to outdoor soil, mud, surface water, or tropical storm conditions is extraordinarily unlikely to have melioidosis.

relationships.target: Normal Inflammatory Markers and Absence of Leukocytosis
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Normal admission inflammatory markers (CRP <10 mg/L, normal procalcitonin) and normal white blood cell count without bandemia effectively excludes acute systemic or invasive melioidosis.

relationships.target: Rapid Clinical Defervescence on Standard Ceftriaxone or Ampicillin
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Prompt clinical defervescence and symptom resolution within 48–72 hours of empirical treatment with ampicillin, ceftriaxone, or cefotaxime definitively excludes Burkholderia pseudomallei due to its uniform intrinsic beta-lactam resistance.

relationships.target: Chronic Indolent Progression Over Months with Mediastinal Lymphadenopathy
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] An indolent constitutional course progressing over multiple months accompanied by prominent hilar and mediastinal lymphadenopathy and normal procalcitonin rules out acute pulmonary melioidosis and indicates primary mycobacterial infection.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Pulmonary tuberculosis closely mimics the upper-lobe cavitary lesions and night sweats of melioidosis, but TB runs an insidious multi-week-to-month course, exhibits normal to mildly elevated WBC, prominent mediastinal lymphadenopathy on chest imaging, and acid-fast bacilli on sputum smear; acute pulmonary melioidosis evolves over days with high neutrophilic leukocytosis (WBC >15,000/µL), massively elevated CRP (>150 mg/L) and procalcitonin, absence of mediastinal adenopathy, and frequent concurrent splenic/prostatic microabscesses.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Community-acquired bacterial pneumonia (Streptococcus pneumoniae, Klebsiella pneumoniae) presents with acute lobar consolidation but responds rapidly within 48–72 hours to empirical ampicillin, ceftriaxone, or respiratory fluoroquinolones; melioidosis is intrinsically resistant to ceftriaxone and penicillins, exhibits a characteristically prolonged fever clearance time (9–10 days on ceftazidime), and frequently presents with multi-organ microabscesses (spleen, liver, prostate) in diabetic hosts.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Leptospirosis shares occupational exposure to wet mud and floodwater, but is distinguished at admission triage by pathognomonic bilateral non-purulent conjunctival suffusion, severe gastrocnemius calf tenderness, direct hyperbilirubinemia with disproportionately mild transaminitis, and rapid defervescence on IV penicillin or doxycycline; it does not produce the multi-organ honeycomb microabscesses (spleen, prostate, parotid) characteristic of melioidosis.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Scrub typhus (Orientia tsutsugamushi) presents with acute tropical fever following outdoor environmental exposure, but is distinguished at admission triage by a pathognomonic necrotic cutaneous eschar, regional lymphadenopathy, frequent sensorineural deafness, and rapid defervescence within 24–48 hours of oral doxycycline; it lacks the necrotizing cavitary pneumonia and deep visceral microabscesses of melioidosis.

relationships.target: Intrinsic Resistance to Ceftriaxone Penicillins and Aminoglycosides
relationships.description: [INTRINSICALLY_RESISTANT_TO] Burkholderia pseudomallei possesses broad, intrinsic multidrug resistance to penicillins, ampicillin, 1st- and 2nd-generation cephalosporins, 3rd-generation cephalosporins (ceftriaxone, cefotaxime), macrolides, aminoglycosides, and colistin; standard empirical sepsis regimens fail and cause clinical progression.

[RESPONDS_TO] High-dose intravenous ceftazidime (2 g IV every 6–8 hours or 50 mg/kg up to 2 g Q8H for ≥10–14 days) is the standard first-line bactericidal acute intensive regimen; median time to defervescence is characteristically prolonged (9–10 days), and persistence of fever during week 1 does not indicate treatment failure.

[RESPONDS_TO] Intravenous meropenem (1–2 g IV every 8 hours) is the preferred carbapenem for critically ill patients presenting with septic shock, deep undrained collections, or neurological melioidosis, providing rapid bactericidal clearance and reduced endotoxin release compared to ceftazidime.

[RESPONDS_TO] Oral co-trimoxazole (TMP-SMX 320/1600 mg twice daily with oral folic acid for a minimum of 3 to 6 months) is the mandatory eradication phase therapy to eliminate intracellular bacterial persisters and prevent late relapse ('Vietnam time-bomb' phenomenon).

relationships.target: Empirical Fluoroquinolone and Macrolide Treatment Failure
relationships.description: [INTRINSICALLY_RESISTANT_TO] Empirical or eradication regimens utilizing fluoroquinolones (ciprofloxacin, ofloxacin) or macrolides (azithromycin) fail clinically, with unacceptably high failure and bacteriological relapse rates (~29%), and should not be used.
